title: Lecture 1 — Practice Exam A: Foundations
subject: Programming Languages
description: Lecture 1 only. Original AI-generated practice questions based on the supplied handout; not an official exam or answer key.

questions.question: Why does studying programming language concepts make learning a new language easier?
options: You can recognize familiar concepts behind unfamiliar syntax
It eliminates the need to learn syntax
It makes all languages behave identically
It guarantees every program is correct
questions.correctAnswer: You can recognize familiar concepts behind unfamiliar syntax
questions.explanation: Conceptual knowledge transfers between languages; the lecture lists easier language learning as a benefit.

questions.question: Which domain in the lecture emphasizes floating-point computations and arrays?
questions.correctAnswer: Scientific applications
questions.explanation: Scientific programs often perform numerical calculations on arrays; Fortran is the lecture's example.

questions.question: Which language is associated with reports, decimal numbers, and character data in the lecture?
questions.correctAnswer: COBOL
questions.explanation: The lecture associates COBOL with business applications and their reporting and decimal-data needs.

questions.question: What does readability measure?
options: How many languages a developer knows
How small the compiler executable is
How easily a program can be read and understood
questions.correctAnswer: How easily a program can be read and understood
questions.explanation: Readability concerns understanding a program, rather than execution speed or tool size.

questions.question: What does writability measure?
options: How easily a language can be used to create programs
How easily source files can be moved between computers
How closely a program follows its specification
How quickly the CPU fetches instructions
questions.correctAnswer: How easily a language can be used to create programs
questions.explanation: Writability is the ease of expressing programs in a language.

questions.question: A program is reliable when it does what?
questions.correctAnswer: Conforms to its specifications
questions.explanation: The lecture defines reliability as performing according to specifications.

questions.question: What is feature multiplicity?
options: Using several source files in a project
Checking several array indices at once
Having several ways to accomplish the same operation
Having many processors in one computer
questions.correctAnswer: Having several ways to accomplish the same operation
questions.explanation: Multiple ways to express the same operation can complicate a language and its readability.

questions.question: Which description best matches orthogonality?
options: Every construct needs a unique exception to the rules
Every program must use exactly one data type
Every operator has exactly one character
Primitive constructs combine according to a small, consistent set of rules
questions.correctAnswer: Primitive constructs combine according to a small, consistent set of rules
questions.explanation: Orthogonality supports predictable combinations of a relatively small set of primitives.

questions.question: Why is a Boolean value helpful for representing a timeout flag?
options: It makes the intended true-or-false meaning clearer
It removes the need for all conditions
It guarantees faster execution on every computer
It prevents the program from ever timing out
questions.correctAnswer: It makes the intended true-or-false meaning clearer
questions.explanation: The lecture contrasts a numeric flag with a Boolean flag to illustrate the readability benefit of suitable data types.

questions.question: What does support for abstraction allow?
options: Skipping type checking in every language
Using complex structures or operations while ignoring internal details
Removing every variable from a program
Replacing all syntax with machine code
questions.correctAnswer: Using complex structures or operations while ignoring internal details
questions.explanation: Abstraction hides details behind structures or operations, making programs easier to express.

questions.question: Which reliability feature can intercept a run-time error and take corrective action?
questions.correctAnswer: Exception handling
questions.explanation: Exception handling provides a way to respond to run-time errors.

questions.question: What is aliasing?
options: Two variables stored in unrelated memory locations
Two programs compiled by the same compiler
Two names for different programming domains
Two or more distinct ways to reference the same memory location
questions.correctAnswer: Two or more distinct ways to reference the same memory location
questions.explanation: Aliasing means different references can access the same location, making changes harder to track.

questions.question: Which cost is especially affected by program readability?
questions.correctAnswer: Maintenance cost
questions.explanation: Maintenance includes correcting and extending programs, which requires understanding existing code.

questions.question: What is portability?
options: The ability to catch every error before execution
The ease of moving programs from one implementation to another
The ability to express an operation in fewer symbols
The precision of a language definition
questions.correctAnswer: The ease of moving programs from one implementation to another
questions.explanation: The lecture ties portability especially to language standardization.

questions.question: In the lecture's model, what do imperative-language variables represent?
questions.correctAnswer: Memory cells
questions.explanation: Imperative languages reflect von Neumann architecture: variables model memory cells.

questions.question: Which language category computes primarily by applying functions to parameters?
questions.correctAnswer: Functional
questions.explanation: Function application is the central computation mechanism in the functional category.

questions.question: Java array-bounds checks illustrate which design trade-off in the lecture?
questions.correctAnswer: Reliability versus execution cost
questions.explanation: Bounds checks improve safety but add work during execution.

questions.question: What is the output of lexical analysis?
questions.correctAnswer: Lexical units
questions.explanation: Lexical analysis converts source characters into lexical units, often called tokens.

questions.question: What is the key idea of a hybrid implementation?
options: Translate all code directly to final machine code before execution
Use markup to replace the operating system
Translate source to an intermediate language, then interpret that form
Execute source with no intermediate translation stage
questions.correctAnswer: Translate source to an intermediate language, then interpret that form
questions.explanation: Hybrid systems combine translation with interpretation of an intermediate representation.

questions.question: When does a preprocessor expand embedded macros?
questions.correctAnswer: Before the program is compiled
questions.explanation: The lecture describes macro processing immediately before compilation, including C include and define directives.
